# Insight cards (generated by cards.py)

Each card follows [ADR 0006](../../../docs/adr/0006-insight-card-contract.md). Ranked by the share of tasks, turns or spend it touches. Numbers with the basis `checked` use the ground truth of the simulation in the place of sampled checks.

| # | Card | Decision | Owner | Basis | Readiness |

## 1. The cost is in the seats, not in the tokens

**Decision.** D1: Which seats do we pay for? **Owner.** finance

**Finding.** Seats cost 304 times the token cost of the work done on them.

**Evidence.**
- Licences in the window: 271.43; token cost at list prices: 0.89
- Per task started: 4.24 of licence against 0.014 of tokens
- Tokens equal the seat price at about 1,702 tasks per seat per month; staff did 2.7 tasks per person per week

**Basis.** `counted`. **Error.** none for the counts; the token cost is list price, not a bill.

**Readiness.** `act` (counted evidence).

**Action.** Manage the number of seats before the token spend. Review token cost only for seats with heavy use.

**Caveat.** The simulated staff are light users. Heavy agent use changes the ratio.

## 2. Atlas gets the most answers right

**Decision.** D3: Which tool for which job? **Owner.** platform owner

**Finding.** Atlas is right on 88% of checked turns, Beacon on 49% and Chatly on 15%.

**Evidence.**
- Checked turns correct: Atlas 66/75, Beacon 37/75, Chatly 11/75
- Atlas against Beacon: +39 points, 95% interval +24 to +53 with the script as the unit
- 31 of 64 tasks started on another platform than Atlas

**Basis.** `checked`. **Error.** sampling interval, 75 checked turns per platform from 32 scripts.

**Readiness.** `act` (D3 bar: the interval of the difference excludes zero with the script as the unit).

**Action.** Make Atlas the default for work that needs company data.

**Caveat.** Every script was run once on every platform. In a company that is a planned test set, not what the traces give for free.

## 3. Quiet seats, not yet unused seats

**Decision.** D1: Which seats do we pay for? **Owner.** finance

**Finding.** 7 of 24 seats had almost no task starts, worth 150 of 570 per month, and 0 of them can be called unused on this evidence.

**Evidence.**
- Quiet seats: hana on Chatly (0 of 6 starts), dmitri on Chatly (0 of 6 starts), ines on Beacon (0 of 1 starts), ines on Chatly (0 of 1 starts), freya on Beacon (0 of 3 starts), freya on Chatly (0 of 3 starts), ben on Atlas (0 of 4 starts)
- A seat with no start is evidence only after its holder has made 29 task starts. The busiest holder made 9; at the observed rates that takes 4 to 56 more weeks
- In a simulation of this company, the 10% share rule flags a seat that is in use in 97% of 2-week windows
- Used only as a fallback after a failure elsewhere: dmitri on Chatly

**Basis.** `linked`. **Error.** task links: precision 13/13, recall 13/13.

**Readiness.** `watch` (D1 bar: the chance of this few starts at a true share of 10% is under 5%).

**Action.** Do not cancel on this evidence. Ask the holders, or wait until the evidence rule fires.

**Caveat.** A holder with one seat is never flagged. A seat used rarely but for something that matters looks the same as an unused one.

## 4. Chatly lacks the MCP server shop

**Decision.** D4: What do we build next: skills, connectors, context? **Owner.** enablement

**Finding.** 11 tasks left Chatly for a platform with the MCP server `shop` or ended there on a reply that says it cannot reach the data.

**Evidence.**
- 3 of 3 tasks that left Chatly used the MCP server shop on the next platform
- Tasks started on Chatly that were re-done elsewhere or ended on trouble: 78% (7/9)
- 8 more tasks ended on Chatly with a reply that says it cannot reach the data; 50% (11/22) of its turns carry such a phrase (the phrase marks a wrong answer in 9 of 10 checked turns)

**Basis.** `linked`. **Error.** task links: precision 13/13, recall 13/13; inability phrase scored above.

**Readiness.** `act` (D4 bar: the same gap in 5 tasks or more is `act`, in 3 or 4 `check first` (here 11)).

**Action.** Add the MCP server `shop` to Chatly, or send that work to a platform that has it.

**Caveat.** The next platform may have used the capability only because it was there. A capability the first platform has but did not use in the window counts as missing.

## 5. Half of the wrong answers leave no sign in the trace

**Decision.** D3: Which tool for which job? **Owner.** platform owner

**Finding.** 19 of 37 turns that failed a check show no error, no empty reply and no "I can't" in the trace.

**Evidence.**
- Silent failures: 51% (19/37), 95% interval 36% to 67%
- A failed tool call marks a wrong answer in 4 of 18 turns; an inability phrase in 11 of 13
- 10 checked turns per platform pick the best platform in 96% of simulated samples: 30 checks for the period

**Basis.** `checked`. **Error.** sampling interval, 134 checked turns.

**Readiness.** `act` (counted against checks; the interval is far from zero).

**Action.** Do not rank platforms by error rates. Fund about 30 checked answers per period, and check flagged turns first.

**Caveat.** Failure rates from flagged turns only are biased upwards. Use a random sample for the rate.

## 6. Work that is done twice

**Decision.** D4: What do we build next: skills, connectors, context? **Owner.** enablement

**Finding.** 13% of the token cost and 8% of people's time went to sessions that the person then re-did on another platform.

**Evidence.**
- Re-done sessions: 13 of 77
- Upper bound with sessions that ended on trouble: 34% of cost, 28% of time
- Highest on Beacon: 28% of its token cost was re-done elsewhere

**Basis.** `linked`. **Error.** task links: precision 13/13, recall 13/13; the trouble flag is right for 9 of 19 sessions, so the upper bound is loose.

**Readiness.** `check first` (linked evidence with a loose upper bound).

**Action.** Start with Beacon: find what its re-done tasks needed (see the capability cards).

**Caveat.** People time is the length of a session, not effort. Tasks dropped with no sign in the trace are not counted.

## 7. Beacon lacks the skill weekly-sales-report

**Decision.** D4: What do we build next: skills, connectors, context? **Owner.** enablement

**Finding.** 3 tasks failed on Beacon, which does not have the skill `weekly-sales-report`.

**Evidence.**
- 3 of 7 tasks that left Beacon used the skill weekly-sales-report on the next platform
- Tasks started on Beacon that were re-done elsewhere or ended on trouble: 41% (9/22)

**Basis.** `linked`. **Error.** task links: precision 13/13, recall 13/13.

**Readiness.** `check first` (D4 bar: the same gap in 5 tasks or more is `act`, in 3 or 4 `check first` (here 3)).

**Action.** Add the skill `weekly-sales-report` to Beacon, or send that work to a platform that has it.

**Caveat.** The next platform may have used the capability only because it was there. A capability the first platform has but did not use in the window counts as missing.

## 8. Not enough checks to route by task type

**Decision.** D3: Which tool for which job? **Owner.** platform owner

**Finding.** 7 of 21 platform comparisons inside a task type hold up, and no task type has a clear best platform other than Atlas.

**Evidence.**
- Comparisons significant at 0.05: 9 of 21; after correction for many tests: 7
- Task types where another platform has the highest rate: none
- 10 checks per platform and task type pick the right platform 9 times in 10 on average: 210 checks. The window produced 134 checkable turns and 16 of 21 cells are short of 10

**Basis.** `checked`. **Error.** sampling interval; cells hold 4 to 16 checked turns.

**Readiness.** `watch` (D3 bar not met inside task types).

**Action.** Do not route by task type yet. Plan a test set of 10 checked tasks per platform and task type.

**Caveat.** The simulation takes each cell's observed rate as the true rate. Smaller real gaps need more checks.

## 9. The work map cannot be compared across platforms yet

**Decision.** D2: What work goes to AI? **Owner.** leadership

**Finding.** The same task gets the same task type on all three platforms in 34% (11/32) of scripts.

**Evidence.**
- Agreement between platforms (kappa): domain 0.44 to 0.85, task type 0.31 to 0.59
- Label equals the designed label: Atlas domain 88% (28/32), task type 66% (21/32), Beacon domain 78% (25/32), task type 59% (19/32), Chatly domain 69% (22/32), task type 50% (16/32)
- The smallest role has 4 people; the minimum group size is 5

**Basis.** `labelled`. **Error.** agreement as above.

**Readiness.** `watch` (D2 bar: kappa 0.6 or more, and groups at or above the minimum size).

**Action.** Show the work map by domain only, and only for platforms whose labels agree. Fix the task type label before it is used across platforms.

**Caveat.** The chat platform's transcripts have no tool lines, so the same work reads differently. Labels come from many small free models.

## No card

- **D5 Where does sensitive work go?** No sensitivity label or policy exists, so no card can be made. A first count: 26 of 77 sessions name an order, ticket or SKU id in a prompt (Atlas 45% (17/38), Beacon 22% (5/23), Chatly 25% (4/16)). An id is not sensitivity.
- **D6 How do I work with AI?** Not an organisation card. The personal report goes to the person (round 3).

Scope of every card: 2 weeks, 12 people, 64 tasks, 77 sessions, 3 platforms.
